TECILCHEM : GETS KERALA NOD FOR 8.08-ACRE COMMERCIAL DEVELOPMENT; MIN RS 10 CR/ACRE INVESTMENT

• Kerala government granted conditional exemption under Section 81(3) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963 for 8.08 acres (3.2600 hectares) of company land
• Land at Nattakam Village, Kottayam Taluk and Kurichi Village, Changanasserry Taluk, Kottayam District
• Exemption is for a proposed residential complex for commercial purposes, commercial establishments, shopping mall, convention centre, hospital and hotel
• Approval conditions require minimum investment of ₹10 Cr per acre and employment for at least 20 persons per acre
• Land must be utilised within two years or the exemption stands forfeited
• Company to seek Industries Department permission to submit a fresh Detailed Project Report given market, technology and industrial changes
Impact: Positive (statutory approval enables land monetisation via commercial and infrastructure development, but subject to a two-year deadline and fresh DPR)

RUBICON : MCA RETURNS FAST-TRACK MERGER APPLICATION WITH KIA HEALTH TECH

• Regional Director, Western Region, MCA returned the fast-track scheme of merger application of KIA Health Tech (wholly owned subsidiary) with the company; order dated November 6, 2026 received on November 13, 2026
• Scheme approved by 88.65% of total shareholders versus 90% required, though 99.44% of shareholders who voted approved it
• Scheme approved by unsecured creditors representing 71.83% of total value versus 90% required; all creditors who responded consented but response levels were short
• Company evaluating options including going through the regular NCLT process
• No material impact on business operations as KIA Health Tech presently has no operations; no financial implications, penalty or restriction stated
Impact: Negative (Fast-track internal restructuring stalled and NCLT route adds timeline; operational and financial impact nil)

ZYDUSLIFE : USFDA INSPECTION AT LIQMEDS UK CLOSES WITH 4 OBSERVATIONS

• USFDA conducted an inspection at Zydus' LiqMeds, UK facility from 9th to 13th November, 2026
• The inspection concluded with 4 observations
• Company said it will closely work with the USFDA to address the observations expeditiously
• Disclosure made under Regulation 30 of SEBI LODR Regulations, 2015
Impact: Negative (Four unresolved observations at the UK site keep a regulatory overhang until they are addressed)

GALAXYSURF : SIGNS MOU WITH LG ELECTRONICS FOR SUSTAINABLE CLEANING SOLUTIONS

• MoU with LG Electronics to co-develop and commercialize next-generation sustainable cleaning solutions
• Collaboration spans LG Advanced Materials leadership team and Galaxy's surfactant expertise
• Executive Director & COO Vaijanath Kulkarni said the partnership marks the beginning of a long-term journey in sustainable cleaning solutions
• No financial value or commercial terms disclosed for the MoU
Impact: Positive (adds a globally respected technology partner and a commercialisation route for sustainable cleaning solutions, though scale and revenue contribution are not yet quantified)

SOLEX : WINS RS 628.37 CR ORDER

• Secured a ₹628.37 Cr order from a global renewable energy group for N-Type TOPCon 615/620 Wp Glass-to-Glass (G12R) solar PV modules, its largest single order in FY27
• Other wins: ₹42.47 Cr and ₹75.96 Cr orders for N-Type TOPCon 620 Wp G12R modules, plus domestic orders aggregating ₹74.77 Cr
• Solex and subsidiary Solex Green Energy secured two orders aggregating ₹194.14 Cr (₹180.98 Cr and ₹13.16 Cr respectively) for TOPCon bifacial Glass-to-Glass modules
• Order book visibility over ₹4,000 Cr, including ~₹1,050 Cr confirmed orders backed by advance payments and ~₹3,000 Cr at advanced closure stage
• Subsidiary approved ₹150 Cr CCD issuance
• Q2 FY27 total revenue ₹274.3 Cr, up 75.8% YoY; PAT ₹3.9 Cr, down 32.7% YoY on lower capacity utilisation and fixed costs
Impact: Positive (record order wins and over ₹4,000 Cr pipeline lift revenue visibility despite Q2 margin and PAT pressure)

CYIENT DLM : SIGNS MOU WITH HINDUSTAN SHIPYARD FOR MARITIME DEFENCE ELECTRONICS

• MoU signed with Hindustan Shipyard Limited (HSL), a Miniratna Category-I defence PSU under the Ministry of Defence
• Partnership to explore collaboration in advanced electronics, embedded systems, power electronics, precision manufacturing, testing and product lifecycle support
• Scope includes indigenisation, obsolescence management, test and support systems, autonomous and unmanned maritime platforms and AI-enabled maintenance
• HSL brings shipbuilding, ship repair and platform integration experience; Cyient DLM brings mission-critical electronics and design-led manufacturing
• Collaboration aimed at supporting the Government of India's Atmanirbhar Bharat indigenisation objectives
• No financial, order or investment value disclosed; framework MoU to evaluate potential areas of cooperation
Impact: Positive (Non-binding framework with a defence shipyard PSU opens indigenisation and lifecycle-support opportunities in a regulated, high-entry-barrier segment, though no order value is disclosed yet)

NAVA : 60 MW ODISHA POWER PLANT RESUMES OPERATIONS

Unit was shut from September 4, 2026 for routine inspection, maintenance and overhauling; 60 MW is part of aggregate installed capacity of 150 MW.

GRETEX : APPOINTED MANAGER TO MONEY MASTERS OPEN OFFER WORTH RS 3.48 CR

Open offer covers up to 26.00% of expanded voting capital, total consideration ~₹3.48 Cr.

SREELEATHERS Q2 FY27 ; MISSES GUIDED REVENUE OF RS 9.88 CR, GUIDES Q3 AT RS 67-70 CR

Q2 revenue ₹83.16 Cr, up 11.3% YoY and 39.5% QoQ, but short of the ~₹86 Cr implied by its 45% QoQ August guidance

Q3 FY27 revenue seen at ₹67-70 Cr, ~12.5% above ₹60.90 Cr in Q3 FY26 but ~17.6% below the September quarter

PAT ₹9.88 Cr up 14.8% YoY; operating EBITDA margin up 33 bps to 16.0%

SRIT : WINS RS 128.93 CR ORDER

• Company received new order worth Qatari Riyals ~50 million (₹1,289.3 Million) from Ooredoo QPSC
• Scope covers managed services for electronic health and information systems for pharmacy and drug control departments
• Order awarded by an international entity; Ooredoo QPSC is a QAR ~42 billion Qatari public shareholding company
• 2 years for managed services on onboarding of hospitals, clinics, health centres and pharmacies
• 3 years for managed services of the e-health eco system and national drug control and roll-out operations
• Contracting parties are Ooredoo QPSC with SRIT's branch in Doha QFC, Qatar
Impact: Positive (Large international managed-services win strengthens SRIT's Qatar e-health footprint and revenue visibility)

WABAG : SAUDI WATER AUTHORITY CANCELS RS 2332 CR DESALINATION ORDER

• Customer notified all tender participants via Etimad portal that the 300 MLD Yanbu sea water desalination tender is cancelled for internal reasons attributable to the Customer
• Original award intimated July 24, 2025 was worth about USD 272 million (SAR 1,019 million / ₹2,332 Cr)
• Scope covered design, engineering, supply, construction and commissioning of the 300 MLD mega desalination plant at Yanbu, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
• Contract was executed on 23 July 2025 and submitted to the Customer for counter-signature and formal commencement of the project
• Company is approaching the Customer to understand the reason in better detail and decide the next course of action
Impact: Negative (cancellation of the ~₹2,332 Cr Saudi order removes a large overseas project from the execution pipeline, with reason and remedy still unclear)

COAL INDIA : FILES RHP FOR MAHANADI COALFIELDS IPO

• RHP dated 13 November 2026 for Mahanadi Coalfields filed with RoC, SEBI, BSE and NSE
• Mahanadi Coalfields is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India
• IPO comprises an offer for sale of up to 661,836,300 equity shares by Coal India
• Offer remains subject to applicable approvals and market conditions
Impact: Positive (OFS route can monetise Coal India's holding in MCL; execution subject to approvals and market conditions)

SRIT : RAISES RS 19.04 CR VIA IPO AT ₹130/SHARE

• Fresh issue of 1.68 Cr equity shares at ₹130 per share, aggregating ₹218.4 Cr
• Shares listed on NSE (SRIT) and BSE (544965) on October 6, 2026
• Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from operations ₹104.70 Cr, up 29.0% YoY; PAT ₹13.74 Cr vs ₹9.94 Cr
• H1 FY27 revenue ₹192.51 Cr vs ₹232.62 Cr in H1 FY26
• Sub-contracting and technical fees cut to 63.0% of revenue in H1 FY27 from 74.2% in H1 FY26
• H1 FY27 operating cash flow ₹86.53 Cr vs outflow of ₹19.04 Cr a year ago; cash ₹108.49 Cr as of September 30, 2026
• No specific revenue or EBITDA margin guidance provided
Impact: Positive (₹218.4 Cr IPO proceeds and a sharp swing to positive operating cash flow support the balance sheet, with Q2 revenue up 29% YoY even as H1 revenue is down YoY)

Resolution passed with 100% of valid votes cast in favour at the NCLT-convened meeting held on Nov 13, 2026; no objections raised by unsecured creditors.

• Valid votes in favour 4,25,64,998, or 99.9442% of votes cast by value; against 23,785 (0.0558%)
• 751 unsecured creditors voted in favour and 2 against; no invalid votes; no objections raised on the scheme
• NCLT Chennai order dated September 30, 2026; 347 unsecured creditors attended the meeting via video conferencing
• Transferee company to honour all payment terms with unsecured creditors; scheme remains subject to NCLT sanction
Impact: Neutral (Creditor approval is a procedural milestone in the amalgamation; completion still hinges on NCLT sanction)

FIRSTCRY: INDIA STEP-DOWN SUBSIDIARY ACQUIRES 100% EQUITY STAKE OF DYNAMIC IT SOLUTION

• Globalbees Brands Private Limited, a material subsidiary of Brainbees Solutions, acquired an additional 10.09% stake in Dynamic IT Solution Private Limited from existing shareholders
• Post-acquisition, Globalbees holding in Dynamic IT rises to 100% from 89.91% (including shares held by its nominee)
• Cash consideration of INR 1.02 Crore; transaction completed November 13, 2026, with no regulatory approvals required
• Dynamic IT sells fitness equipment and sports products under the brand Strauss; turnover was ₹11.92 Cr in FY25 and ₹27.4 Cr in FY24, with nil in FY26
• The Strauss brand across all Globalbees subsidiaries combined generated turnover of more than ₹23.14 Cr in FY25
Impact: Positive (full ownership of the Strauss brand consolidates Globalbees' sports and fitness portfolio, though the ₹1.02 Cr outlay limits near-term earnings impact)

ALMONDZ : ASSOCIATE WINS 12.82 CRORE LITRES ETHANOL ALLOCATION FROM OMCS

• Associate Premier Green Innovations (PGIPL) secured 12.82 crore litres of ethanol allocation for ESY 2026-27
• Allocation split: 6.44 crore litres for Himachal Pradesh plant and 6.38 crore litres for the newly commissioned Odisha plant
• Odisha plant allocation is about 97% of its 6.60 crore litre capacity in its first supply year
• PGIPL secured about 87% of its offered 14.77 crore litres in a tender where industry offered 1,932 crore litres against OMC requirement of 1,100 crore litres
• PGIPL expects to nearly double revenue in the next financial year with both plants supplying
• Almondz Global Securities holds 40.99% of PGIPL's total equity
Impact: Positive (Associate's near-full capacity allocation across both plants supports volume-led revenue growth, though benefits accrue to Almondz via its 40.99% associate stake)

text:
Direct Tax Collections Rise 11.8%

India's net direct tax collections grew by 11.8% year-on-year to ₹14.42 lakh crore as of November 10, outpacing the budgeted growth pace.

Growth was heavily driven by corporate tax collections and a 51.6% surge in securities transactions tax (STT), reflecting strong activity in the financial markets.

South Korean Auto Parts Makers Plan ₹1,370-cr Investment in TN

South Korean auto component makers Hwashin and Seoyon have proposed a ₹1,370 crore investment in Tamil Nadu over the next five years to ramp up manufacturing and tech.

Hwashin plans to invest ₹850 crore for R&D and capacity expansion, while Seoyon E-Hwa is committing ₹520 crore toward tech upgrades and new business development.

**CLSA ON TATA POWER – HOLD | TARGET ₹415**

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Recurring PAT grew 51% YoY.
- Performance was broadly in-line with estimates.
- Indonesian coal supported earnings growth.
- Lower base benefited Mundra performance.
- Wind generation improved due to climatic conditions.
- Solar EPC and RE IPP PAT declined.

**Margin Pressure**
- Solar module and cell margins impacted 257 bps.
- Solar EPC margins remained under pressure.
- EPC margin decline stood at 410 bps.
- Continued margin pressure remains a concern.

**Key Positives**
- Indonesian coal mines PAT/tonne increased sevenfold.
- Higher seaborne coal prices drove profitability.
- Wind IPP business delivered strong performance.

**Key Monitorables**
- Solar manufacturing margin recovery.
- Solar EPC margin improvement.
- Renewable curtailment and IPP profitability.

**Impact: Mixed**

**JPM ON TATA POWER – NEUTRAL | TARGET ₹423**

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Reported broadly healthy quarterly results.
- Growth remained broad-based across businesses.
- JV/associate profits rose to ₹490 crore.
- Previous year JV profits: ₹130 crore.
- Higher Indonesian coal prices drove growth.

**Capex & Execution**
- 1H capex reached ₹10,000 crore.
- FY27 capex guidance: ₹25,000 crore.
- FY26 actual capex stood at ₹13,000 crore.
- Renewable commissioning guidance retained at 2.5 GW.
- Around 700 MW commissioned during 1H.

**Positive Factors**
- Improved project execution.
- Strong solar manufacturing profitability.
- Healthy regulated business growth.

**Key Risks**
- Singapore case outcome remains crucial.
- Contingent liability stands at US$650 million.
- Valuations offer limited upside.

**Impact: Mixed**

**CITI ON TATA POWER – BUY | TARGET ₹525**

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- Revenue grew 26% YoY to ₹19,700 crore.
- EBITDA increased 11% to ₹3,900 crore.
- PAT surged 36% to ₹1,250 crore.
- PAT beat estimates by 9%.
- Higher coal-associate profits aided PAT growth.

**Broad-Based Business Improvement**
- Improvement across thermal generation and coal.
- Renewables and regulated T&D also improved.
- Odisha DISCOM and transmission earnings grew.
- Mundra turned a modest contributor.

**Capex & Renewable Outlook**
- FY27 capex target retained at ₹25,000 crore.
- ₹10,000 crore capex incurred during 1H.
- Renewable commissioning target remains 2.5 GW.
- Only 645 MW commissioned during 1H.
- Transmission delays shifted execution into 2H.
- Renewable curtailment increased to 11%.
- Curtailment partly offset capacity additions.

**Key Monitorables**
- Back-ended renewable commissioning execution.
- Mundra SPPA closure remains important.
- Portfolio earnings transition is broadening.

**Impact: Positive**

**GOLDMAN SACHS ON SBI – BUY | TARGET ₹1,130**

**Strategic Priorities**
- Focus on self-employed personal loans.
- Expand wealth management offerings.
- Deepen corporate and retail relationships.
- Improve cross-selling opportunities.
- Modernise operations through AI and digital initiatives.

**Credit Growth Outlook**
- Credit growth guidance maintained at 15%.
- Potential to outperform guidance by few percentage points.
- System credit growth currently stands at 18–19%.
- Strong previous-year base limits comparable growth.

**Key Takeaway**
- Focus on cross-selling and business diversification.
- AI and digital initiatives support modernisation.
- Credit growth outlook remains comfortable.

**CLSA ON SBI – OUTPERFORM | TARGET ₹1,325**

**Loan Growth & Outlook**
- Loan growth guidance maintained at 14–15%.
- RAM share targeted at 65% of domestic loans.
- Corporate capex improving in select sectors.
- Mid-corporate capex remains modest.

**Profitability & RoA**
- Core RoA target: 1% over the cycle.
- Fee income and liability management drive improvement.

**Deposit Growth**
- Current account deposit growth remains weak.
- Government deposit run-down impacted CA growth.

**Key Takeaway**
- Management remains positive on SBI's prospects.
- Focus remains on loan growth and RoA improvement.

**GOLDMAN SACHS – FEDERAL BANK | BUY | TARGET ₹430**

**Management's RoA Targets**
- Q2 FY27 RoA stood at 1.3%.
- Immediate RoA target: 1.5%.
- Long-term RoA aspiration: 1.6–1.8%.

**Key RoA Improvement Drivers**
- Strengthening the liability franchise.
- Gradual diversification towards higher-yielding assets.
- Focus on mid-to-high yielding segments.
- Increasing fee income contribution.

**Acquisition & Growth Strategy**
- Prioritising core business strengthening.
- Open to smaller strategic acquisitions.
- Avoiding large-scale mergers currently.
- Large mergers could prolong integration.
- Integration risks could disrupt core performance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Focus remains on improving return ratios.
- Liability franchise and asset mix remain priorities.
- Smaller acquisitions preferred over large mergers.
- RoA improvement remains the key monitorable.
- Goldman Sachs Rating: **BUY**
- Target Price: **₹430**

UBS on Triveni Eng
Buy, TP Rs 840

Q2FY27: Order inflow up 17% YoY (+24% vs street), rev/EBITDA down 3/45%YoY; missed street by 14%/30%

Q2 orders strong at Rs7.6bn (+17% YoY), led by exports (+50%) & domestic pickup Margin:13% (-970bps YoY) due to mix/RM inflation

Mgt expects strong H2 on better execution/mix 

Order strength supports outlook; 

weak margins may weigh on stock near term

Nomura on Insurance
private India life insurers’ individual annualized premium equivalent (APE) was up 6% y-y (on a base of 15%), supported by volume (number of
policies – NOP) growth of 5% y-y (on a base of 10%).

On a total APE basis, private players witnessed growth of 20% y-y (on a base of 13%) in Oct-26.

For covered life insurers, total APE growth in Oct-26 was fastest for 

HDFC Life at 16% y-y followed by Axis Max Life at 14% y-y & ICICI Life at 9% y-y

SBI Life’s total APE was soft at 2% y-y (on a high base of 19%)

Draft on distribution reform is 
awaited, and should likely be next trigger for sector

CLSA on Lemon Tree
O-p, TP Rs 163

Reported a record 2QFY27, with revenue above estimates led by increases in both ARR and occupancy.

Margin (beat) improved YoY despite the GST impact and provision for SAR.

It remains on track to open c.2,000 keys in FY27 with pace to accelerate from FY28 onwards.

It signed an MoU with Omaxe in 2Q to manage its upcoming c.4000 keys (one of largest single contracts).

LT expects margins to improve as its major renovation nears completion and operating leverage from upcoming keys

Nomura on GE Shipping
Buy, TP Rs 1995
In-line 2QFY27 with strong NAV growth
Expect strong 3Q on record-high tanker rates; trading at attractive 0.52x ex-cash NAV
Raise FY27/28F PAT by 11%/7%

JPMORGAN ON OIL MARKETING COMPANIES (OMCs) 

POSITIVE OUTLOOK | PREFERS BPCL & IOCL

• Maintains constructive outlook on OMC sector; BPCL and Indian Oil (IOCL) remain preferred picks.

• Sustained decline in crude oil prices could trigger FY28 earnings upgrades across OMCs.

• Every $10/barrel annualised decline in crude prices could boost combined EBITDA by ₹70,000–80,000 Cr.

• Reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and higher global oil supply remain key catalysts; potential excise-duty reversals pose a risk.

UBS ON BHARAT ELECTRONICS

• Rating: BUY | Target Price: ₹550 (Earlier: ₹500)

• ₹2.5 lakh Cr order pipeline over FY27–30 supports potential fresh order inflows of ₹2 lakh Cr.

• Expects 18% revenue and earnings CAGR through FY30, driven by radar, missile and electronic warfare programmes.

• Strong systems-integration capabilities limit competitive risks.

• UBS raises FY29 EPS estimates by 3%.

UBS ON TRIVENI TURBINE

• Rating: BUY | Target Price: ₹840

• Strong order inflows, driven by exports and improving domestic demand, support medium-term execution visibility.

• Management expects stronger H2 FY27 performance, supported by improved execution and favourable product mix.

• Raw material costs and product mix remain near-term margin pressure risks despite healthy order momentum.

MORGAN STANLEY ON INDIA LIFE INSURANCE SECTOR

• Maintains an attractive outlook on the life insurance sector.

• HDFC Life and Axis Max Life outperform in retail premium growth.

• SBI Life and ICICI Prudential Life witness relatively subdued retail premium growth.

• Group insurance business supports overall APE growth despite modest individual premium expansion.

• Sustained recovery in retail premiums remains key to strengthening underlying sector growth momentum.

Goldman Sacs on SBI ; Buy TP Rs 1130

Chairman articulated his vision for bank which included increased focus on self-employed personal loans, expansion into wealth management offerings, deepening corporate & retail relationships to maximize cross sell, & modernizing operating model through AI and digital initiatives

Bank remains comfortable with its credit growth outlook, maintaining guidance of 15%, with potential to outperform by a few percentage points.

While system credit growth has been running at 18-19% currently, management believes the exceptionally strong base of the previous year makes it difficult for bank to achieve growth in-line with system.

CLSA on SBI ; O-P TP Rs 1325

US roadshow takeaways

Management was positive on banking sector and SBI’s prospects in general.

There is some corporate capex in sectors like thermal & renewable power and roads.

However, mid-corporate capex is still modest.

SBI reiterated its 14-15% loan growth guidance with the share of RAM (retail, agri, MSME) at 65% of domestic loans.

ROA is a key focus area and management targets 1% core ROA over the cycle.

Levers for improvement would be fee income and liability management.

On deposit front, management attributed weak current account (CA) deposit growth to a run-down in government deposits.

Goldman Sacs on Federal BK ; Buy, TP Rs 430

Management remains focused on improving its RoA from 1.3% in 2QFY27 towards its immediate target of 1.5%.

Over long term, bank aspires to clock RoAs of 1.6-1.8%

Improvement will be driven by a combination of liability franchise strengthening, gradual asset-mix diversification towards mid-high yielding segments and higher fee income.

Management articulated its thought process of strengthening its core business and looking at smaller acquisitions, with intent to strengthening the core instead of any big bang merger where integration could take longer and derail banks core performance.

CLSA on Tata Power ; Hold, TP Rs 415

2Q recurring PAT was up 51% YoY, in-line with estimate.

It was driven by Indonesia coal, a low base with shutdown of Mundra & a climate driven turnaround in wind generation pulled back by a decline in PAT for solar EPC and a weak solar renewable energy (RE) IPP business due to curtailment

Surprise in 2Q was a 257bp margin impact for solar module & cell business & continued pressure on EPC margins of 410bps, a key long-term catalyst.

Bright spots were the Indonesian coal mines’ PAT/t rising 7x YoY on a rise in seaborne coal prices & wind IPP business, which did well due to climate changes

JPMorgan on Tata Power ; Neutra; TP Rs 423

Reported broadly healthy 2QFY27 results.

Growth was broad-based, aided by increased profits in coal SPVs. Share of JV/associate profits spiked to Rs4.9bn from Rs1.3bn y/y, driven by higher realised coal prices at Indonesian mines. 

Capex in 1HFY27 was Rs100bn (vs FY27 guidance of Rs250bn, FY26A: Rs130bn) indicating improved execution, and management reiterated its commissioning guidance of 2.5GW (1H ~700MW).

Improved execution, strong profitability in solar manufacturing, and healthy growth in regulated businesses are encouraging
Outcome of the case in Singapore (contingent liability of US$650mn) is key to watch

Valuations leave limited upside.

Goldman Sacs on Garden Reach ; Sell, TP Rs 1735

Q2FY27 missed estimates on Revenue and EPS

Post receipt of Next-Gen Covette (NGC) order worth INR 320bn (GRSE's share), stock has done well; however, concerns around revenue declining post FY28E still persist.

Besides, beyond delivery of last ship of P-17A program in Q3FY27, do not see any major deliveries in near term.

This is likely to impact margins as well post FY27.

Taking cognizance of higher than estimated order value of INR 320bn (GSe: INR 290bn), raise our FY27E/FY28E EPS by 4%/6%
Your actions are the key to overcoming anything: obstacles, outdated beliefs, and self-imposed limits.

**Announcement** 📢

**Veefin Solutions has officially commenced trading on the NSE and BSE main boards!**

What makes this particularly interesting is that the company is simultaneously making a strategic shift towards AI with its new identity, **veefin.ai**.

Building on its enterprise technology business, Veefin is expanding into AI with AIOS, a platform that deploys digital employees across industries and business functions. It has already developed over 1,000 reusable AI skills and begun internal deployments.

Another interesting aspect is its financial performance. For H1 FY27, Veefin reported:

• Group Revenue: ₹238.82 crore, up 116.2%
• Group PAT: ₹24.85 crore, up 126.6%
• Standalone Revenue: ₹49.19 crore, up 83.6%
• Standalone PAT: ₹13.97 crore, up 79.4%

An interesting combination of strong business growth, main board listing and an ambitious AI strategy.

Definitely a company worth keeping on the radar.

• Nifty Target – Raises December 2026 target to 26,100 from 25,000.

• Ratings – Maintains near-term Trading Buy and 12-month Neutral stance.

• Near-Term Outlook – Easing Iran tensions, softer crude prices, lower bond yields and improving flows support a market rally.

• Earnings – Strong earnings momentum provides temporary support, but weak demand and limited earnings upgrades raise sustainability concerns.

• Medium-Term Risks – Expensive valuations, fiscal constraints and AI-related risks cloud the outlook.

• Preferred Sector – Financials remain Bernstein's preferred sector.

• Key Triggers – Potential AI-trade reversal, equity tax relief, resilient domestic macro, reasonable large-cap valuations and light positioning could sustain inflows.

• Large-Cap Focus – Large caps could be the cleaner play on a revival in FPI flows.

• Valuations – Large-cap valuations have become more reasonable.

• Key Rationale – Higher liquidity and greater FPI ownership make large caps more direct beneficiaries of returning foreign flows.

text: Neogen Chem - Antique IC.pdf

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.
